title: TUI: follow up held-Enter handling for AltGr and app-level shortcuts
body:
Independent Opus 5.5 High review approved #2405 at 07b47c4d78de386b0720d369764df0ca3a1b2f01 with no blocking defects, and recorded these follow-ups:

1. **AltGr at the start of a pasted second line on Windows.** Type a >=16-character raw burst, Enter, then an AltGr-generated character inside the 32 ms lookahead. The new outer cancellation guards use `modifiers.intersects(CONTROL | ALT)`, whereas the composer uses the AltGr-aware `key_hint::has_ctrl_or_alt`. The outer guard can cancel the held Enter and lose the newline. The pre-fix branch submitted the first line prematurely in this case; #2405 improves grouping but does not cover this modifier variant. Align the four consumer guards with the composer and add controlled-clock Windows coverage.

2. **App-level shortcuts inside the lookahead.** Ctrl+T (transcript) and Ctrl+G (external editor) are intercepted above ChatWidget. If invoked inside the roughly 32 ms window after an ambiguous Enter, Ctrl+T can leave submission armed until the overlay closes, and Ctrl+G can seed the editor without the buffered draft. Cancel/materialize the held input before these app-level transitions and cover them with a controlled clock.

3. **Module wording.** Clarify `paste_burst.rs`: an explicit paste during lookahead cancels the *submission* and preserves the held Enter as a newline; it does not discard that Enter.

These are source-review findings, not claimed native Windows or external-editor reproductions. The fix in #2405 has separate passing controlled-clock and PTY evidence for ordinary raw-key multiline paste, single-line submission, bracketed paste, Escape/Ctrl+C cancellation, and recovery.
